data.name: Estonia
data.summary: Flat 22% income tax in 2026 (planned rise to 24% cancelled in Dec 2025); capital gains taxed at 22% but deferrable indefinitely through the investment account; foreign portfolio dividends generally exempt; no inheritance, gift or wealth tax. Companies pay 22/78 only on distribution.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Ordinary Estonian tax residence; no special regime for new arrivals exists.
regimes.eligibility: Tax residence via permanent home in Estonia or more than 183 days in any 12-month period.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are ordinary income taxed at the flat 22% rate (2026). Gains reinvested inside an 'investment account' (investeerimiskonto) are deferred until withdrawals exceed contributions, which makes long-term deferral possible for a listed-securities portfolio.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Basic exemption EUR 8,400/yr (irrelevant at this wealth level). Gain on sale of own home used as residence is exempt (general rule; not re-verified here). Losses on securities offset only securities/capital gains and may be carried forward.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Investment account available only to Estonian tax residents; account may be with a bank/investment firm in the EEA or an OECD state. Assets must be bought with money from the account.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Flat personal income tax 22% for 2026 (EMTA tax-rates page, checked 15 Oct 2026). There is no 2% surcharge in 2026: the security (defence) tax planned for 2026-2028, which included a 2% levy on income and a 2% tax on company profits, was scrapped by the government on 8 May 2025 before it took effect (ERR); the rise to 24% legislated in its place was cancelled in December 2025, and EMTA lists 22% and CIT 22/78 for 2026 with no surcharge. Professional/business activity (registered sole trader) is taxed with social tax; a passive investor is not.

sources.title: Estonia - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Exact current text of Income Tax Act § 17 (investment account) and § 15 (gains) not opened in Riigi Teataja (site is JS-rendered); relied on EMTA guidance.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Flat 22% PIT on net gain (2026), no holding-period relief. Effective rate can be deferred to near 0% in present-value terms via the investment account until money is withdrawn beyond contributions.
capital_gains.professional_trader: No separate trader regime for individuals; a business conducted as a sole proprietor (FIE) adds social tax 33% on business income.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents taxed on worldwide gains; foreign tax credit limited to Estonian tax (22%) per country.

dividends.summary: Dividends from Estonian companies carry no personal income tax: the company pays 22/78 corporate income tax when it distributes. Foreign dividends are exempt for a resident individual if foreign tax was withheld on the dividend or the underlying profit was taxed abroad (PwC); otherwise 22%.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Domestic dividends: no PIT (except 7% WHT on redistribution of dividends that were taxed at the old 14/86 rate before 2025).
dividends.important_exceptions: The 14/86 reduced CIT rate on regular dividends and the related 7% WHT on individuals were abolished from 1 January 2025 (EMTA). Flat personal income tax 22% for 2026 (EMTA tax-rates page). A rise to 24% from 2026, legislated in 2025 when the planned security (defence) tax was abolished, was cancelled by amendments adopted by the Riigikogu in December 2025 (reported by secondary sources; EMTA lists 22% for 2026).

sources.title: Estonia - Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties

open_questions: Foreign-dividend exemption for individuals taken from PwC 'Income determination'; statutory text (Income Tax Act § 18) not opened. Confirm whether a US dividend with only 15% treaty WHT qualifies as fully exempt (expected yes).
dividends.rate_basis: domestic_rate 0: tax borne by the company at 22/78 (=28.2% of net dividend). foreign_gross_rate 0: exempt where source WHT was withheld or underlying profit taxed, which covers ordinary listed foreign shares; 22% with credit otherwise. Foreign dividends are exempt for a resident individual when income tax was withheld abroad or paid on the underlying profit (EMTA, 'Income derived in a foreign state': declared in table 8.8, not taxed in Estonia whatever the foreign tax); only dividends with no foreign tax are taxed at 22%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Dividends paid by Estonian companies carry company-level CIT 22/78 on distribution; no additional WHT on dividends to non-residents in the standard case (7% WHT only for redistributed pre-2025 14/86 profits).
dividends.treaty_network: Broad treaty network with EU/OECD states and the US (exact count not verified); foreign tax credit is limited to the Estonian tax per country.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Modelled as the structure regime 'oue_holding': an Estonian OÜ pays no tax on dividends or gains it keeps; 22/78 of the net amount is due when it distributes (Income Tax Act § 50(1)), with no further personal tax on a resident shareholder.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no recurring levy on financial assets.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Annual municipal land tax 0.1%-1% of assessed land value; no tax on buildings. Land under the home up to a size limit is exempt.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax and no gift tax. Inherited assets are not income for the heir. A later sale is taxed as a capital gain using the deceased's acquisition cost.

regimes.name: Estonian holding company (osaühing, OÜ)
regimes.description: The family holds the portfolio through an Estonian private limited company (OÜ) owned by the parents. Estonia taxes a company's profit only when it is distributed (22/78 of the net distribution, Income Tax Act § 50(1)), so dividends and gains the OÜ earns and keeps are untaxed, and a portfolio can compound without annual tax. Distributing 78 costs 22 of company tax and nothing further for a resident individual shareholder (since 1 January 2025 dividends are taxed only at company level). Wealth tax (none) and inheritance tax (none) are the same as for direct holding, so those metrics inherit from the standard regime.
regimes.eligibility: Any person can found an OÜ (notarised or e-filed articles, commercial register entry, share capital as set by the Commercial Code). The shareholders must be Estonian tax residents to get the personal-side treatment modelled here. Contributing an existing portfolio in kind may be a disposal for the individual taxed at 22% on the built-in gain (not verified in the statute), so the structure is cheapest funded with cash or newly bought positions.
regimes.duration_note: A company under ordinary law with no time limit; it lasts as long as the OÜ exists. The distribution-based system has no sunset in the sources read.

structure.payout_notes: Company-level income tax of 22/78 of the net distribution (Income Tax Act § 50(1), rate in § 4), i.e. 22% of the cash the company uses (EUR 78 paid out costs EUR 22 of tax on a EUR 100 outlay), so the rate is 0.22 of the gross outlay. No personal income tax and no withholding on dividends to resident individuals from 1 January 2025 (the 14/86 rate and the 7% withholding were abolished; the 7% applies only to legacy lower-taxed profits). Distributions include deemed ones (expenses without a business purpose, gifts, fringe benefits, transfer-pricing adjustments). Reductions of share capital and liquidation proceeds are taxed differently and were not researched. The planned 2% defence/security tax was scrapped in 2025 (see the standard regime notes).
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: No substance test is needed for a resident OÜ holding a portfolio. Deemed distributions (non-business expenses, loans to shareholders on non-market terms, private use of company assets) are taxed at 22/78 when they arise. Dividends from foreign companies received by an OÜ are exempt from the CIT charge on onward distribution only where the OÜ holds at least 10% and (outside the EEA and Switzerland) the profit was taxed abroad or tax was withheld (PwC); portfolio stakes below 10% therefore get no such relief, but this is irrelevant while profits are retained. Foreign withholding tax on the portfolio's dividends is assumed lost inside the OÜ: PwC says certain foreign taxes can be credited against the 22/78 charge, but conditions were not found. CFC rules do not arise for a resident company.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Not researched in the statute. Retained profits are taxed only when paid out, so a family leaving Estonia keeps the same deferral inside the OÜ; any exit tax on the shares of an individual who emigrates was not found. Liquidation proceeds and capital reductions above paid-in capital are taxed as distributions (not verified).

capital_gains.summary: Gains the OÜ realises on shares, funds and other assets are not taxed when realised: Estonian corporate income tax falls only on distributions. Selling and reinvesting inside the company therefore costs nothing until money is paid out.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: No holding period or minimum stake for retained gains. Distribution tax of 22/78 applies to whatever is paid out, whether it comes from gains or dividends.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Payout at 22/78 is in the structure terms, not in these rates. A planned rise of the rate to 24/76 for 2026 was cancelled (EMTA lists 22/78).

open_questions: Income Tax Act § 50 (text on Riigi Teataja) was not opened; relied on EMTA's dividends page (which cites § 50(1), § 4(1),(11)) and PwC.
capital_gains.rate_basis: 0%: retained profit and gains are exempt in an Estonian company until distributed (PwC: 'all undistributed corporate profits are tax exempt'; gains on all asset types are exempt while undistributed). The 22/78 charge on paying them out is the structure's payout rate.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Not relevant: a company's trading profit is likewise untaxed until distributed.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide gains of the company are exempt until distribution.

dividends.summary: Dividends the OÜ receives, from Estonian or foreign companies, are not taxed while the profit stays in the company; tax of 22/78 arises only when the OÜ distributes. Foreign withholding on the portfolio's dividends (15% for most) is treated as a final cost inside the OÜ.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Relief on onward distribution of received dividends needs a stake of at least 10% (PwC); not relevant for a diversified portfolio.
dividends.important_exceptions: If the foreign withholding can in fact be credited against the 22/78 charge on distribution (PwC mentions credits but gives no conditions), the OÜ would be slightly better off than modelled.

dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding on dividends to resident individuals from 2025; the company pays 22/78 on distribution.

income.name: Estonia

income_tax.summary: Flat 22% on all income of residents; minimum monthly basic allowance EUR 700 from 1 Jan 2026, applicable to everybody, with no phase-out. Employee: unemployment insurance 1.6% (no cap stated) and, for those born after 1982, 2% (or 4% or 6%) to the funded pension; health cover comes from the employer's 33% social tax. The recorded 3.6% is 1.6% plus the 2% minimum pension contribution.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Sole proprietors pay 33% social tax on net business income (after deductible business expenses; cash-basis accounting). Maximum 2026 liability EUR 36,867.60, equal to a business income of EUR 111,720 (computed: 36,867.60 / 0.33), which is the recorded cap. EMTA's page (re-read 2026-10-15) states the 33% rate and the 2026 maximum of EUR 36,867.60, computed on monthly bases of EUR 8,860 for the first three months and EUR 9,460 for the other nine (EUR 111,720); it gives no minimum. Self-employed also pay 22% income tax on net business income.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal income tax in the PwC page.

regimes.name: Digital Nomad Visa (D visa, temporary stay)
regimes.description: Long-stay (D) visa up to 365 days for people working remotely for a foreign employer, their own foreign company or mainly foreign clients. Income threshold EUR 4,500 a month, shown for the six months before applying (e-Residency FAQ: 'gross of tax', a EUR 150-a-day benchmark, evidence from the past six months; the e-Residency visa page: 'EUR 4,500 net/monthly'). Cannot be renewed: a second visa of up to six months can follow, so total stay is 1.5 years. More than 183 days in 12 months makes the holder an Estonian tax resident taxed at 22%. It is not a residence permit and e-Residency gives no right of residence.

succession.name: Estonia
succession.summary: Descendants, parents and a spouse who depended on the deceased for maintenance can claim half of their intestate share in money. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Estonia has no trust law; foundations exist, but private-benefit use is not confirmed.
succession.reserved_share: Descendants, parents and spouse who would inherit on intestacy and to whom the testator owed maintenance at death: a money claim for half the value of their intestate share (Law of Succession Act, reserved share; e-Justice page cites no article).
succession.foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
succession.trust_note: Estonia is not in the HCCH table for the 1985 Trusts Convention. The sources found do not say how foreign trusts are treated. Foundations (sihtasutus) are governed by the Foundations Act; whether purely private-benefit ones are allowed was not confirmed. A private foundation form has been discussed in commentary but enactment was not found.
open_questions: Whether the Foundations Act allows foundations for private (family) benefit, and whether a separate private foundation form has been enacted (Ecovis commentary only), were not confirmed.
How foreign trusts are recognised and taxed in Estonia was not sourced.

assumptions: The family are Estonian tax residents from arrival (permanent home in Estonia; Income Tax Act residence test) and EU citizens needing no permit.
Personal path: the standard (ordinary) system, with gains taxed when realised. The investment account is not modelled (see open questions).
OÜ path: funded with cash or newly bought positions; the OÜ distributes only what the family spends (EUR 400,000 a year net) and keeps and compounds the rest untaxed.
Foreign dividends carry 15% withholding in the checks; it is lost inside the OÜ and, for the personal path, is taken as the reason the dividend is exempt.
The 2026 rates are 22% income tax and 22/78 company tax: the rise to 24% was cancelled and the 2% defence tax was scrapped in 2025 (EMTA tax-rates page, Ministry of Finance page updated 22.04.2026).
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the investment account (Income Tax Act § 17^1 and § 17^2, EMTA 'Securities and investment account'): gains, dividends and interest earned inside the account are not taxed; income arises only when payments out of the account exceed the sum of earlier contributions (cumulative, date by date, § 17^2). With a EUR 30m contribution and EUR 400,000 withdrawn a year, withdrawals would not pass the contributions for decades, so the gains tax could be deferred for the whole projection; the engine taxes realised gains each year and has no contribution ledger. The account is for residents only and, in general, assets must be bought with money inside it (EMTA names inherited, gifted and liquidation securities as exceptions), so an existing portfolio would have to be sold and the cash contributed.

Foreign dividends of a resident individual: PwC says exempt when tax was withheld abroad or the profit was taxed abroad; EMTA's English page for securities says foreign tax is credited against the Estonian tax and any shortfall is payable (22% less 15% leaves 7%, EUR 14,000 on a EUR 200,000 dividend). The Income Tax Act text was not opened (Riigi Teataja is JS-rendered). The personal check takes the PwC reading; if the other reading is right, expected becomes 47,000 and the tax file changes to credit method at 22%.

Whether the 15% foreign withholding on the OÜ's portfolio dividends can be credited against the 22/78 distribution charge (PwC says certain foreign taxes can) was not found in a source; the OÜ check ignores it.
The OÜ's running costs (accountant, annual report) are not in the tax file, so the OÜ check carries none.

Structures considered and not modelled: a private family foundation or trust (not researched, not known to be commonly used in Estonia). Funding the OÜ with an existing portfolio in kind may be a disposal taxed at 22% (not verified).

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary residence)
paths.note: Flat 22% income tax on realised gains (no holding-period relief); dividends from foreign companies are taken as exempt when tax was withheld abroad (PwC; EMTA's English page reads this differently, see the open questions). No wealth, inheritance or gift tax. The investment account (investeerimiskonto) would defer the gains tax until withdrawals exceed contributions, but the engine cannot express that, so it is not a path.

paths.name: Estonian holding company (OÜ)
paths.note: The OÜ pays no tax on dividends and gains it retains; 22/78 of the net amount is due only when it distributes (Income Tax Act § 50(1)), with no further personal tax on a resident shareholder. The parents' estate holds the OÜ shares at about the portfolio's value; Estonia has no inheritance or gift tax, so there is no business-relief question.

immigration.name: Estonia
immigration.summary: EU citizens register their residence. Non-EU nationals can get a large-investor permit with EUR 1 million in an Estonian company or fund, a business permit with EUR 65,000 in a company you hold shares in, a startup visa, or a digital nomad D visa for remote workers earning about EUR 4,500 a month gross (sources conflict). There is no passive-income or retiree permit found.
immigration.naturalisation: Eight years of residence, the last five on a permanent basis, Estonian at B1, and an exam on the Constitution and Citizenship Act. Time on the digital nomad visa gives no residence credit.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Naturalised citizens generally must renounce their former citizenship (Citizenship Act); exceptions and ancestry claims not verified (secondary sources).
